 'Carrick should be given more time' published at 19:52 GMT 19:52 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Dion Dublin 
Former Coventry and Aston Villa striker on BBC Sport 
 Carrick has said they need to cut out the individual errors, and he’s right. It’s about concentration. It’s about leadership. It's about talking to your team-mate in a way that he understands that you're talking to him like that because you want to win the game. You need to get a hold of your team-mates and be strong with them, tell them ‘we’re not doing enough, lads’. You need to point fingers sometimes.
 Clubs like Manchester United have to have a plan in a situation like this. Otherwise, it's awful management of the football club and the football team. I don't think the answer is getting rid of Carrick. What happens next? You've still got the same group of players that are crossing the white line and representing the football club.
 You can't change all the players. It's too difficult. You can change the manager. It's one person. But is it correcting the issue? Is it correcting the long-term problems? I think Carrick should be given more time.

 Grim reading for Man Utd fans published at 19:49 GMT 19:49 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Manchester United will end tonight 18th in the Premier League, their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th. They've gone eight Premier League games without a win for just the second time, also doing so in April-May 2025.
 They have failed to win in their last eight games in the Premier League, their last joint-longest winless streak was from 1 April 2025 to 16 May 2025.
 United are now guaranteed to spend at least 15 consecutive days in the Premier League relegation zone before they face Liverpool in a fortnight. It'll be their longest run of days in the top-flight drop zone since September-October 1986 (28 days).
 Manchester United have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their first 10 league games in a season for the first time since 1986-87.

 'Man Utd giving themselves a mountain to climb in every game' published at 19:46 GMT 19:46 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Dion Dublin 
Former Coventry and Aston Villa striker on BBC Sport 
 Manchester United clearly still have issues that need sorting. Over the last two games they have overturned two-goal deficits on three occasions to get something out of matches against Roma and Aston Villa. 
 But there's only so many times you can do that because it's quite tiring, physically and mentally. The players today were walking around after the game like they had lost, even though they got a point.
 By starting so slowly they are giving themselves a mountain to climb in every game. The emotions we saw at full-time were relief. I don’t think they are going into the game thinking about Michael Carrick and his job, they are just trying to get three points. But they just don’t seem to be gelling at the moment. There’s not enough energy.
 Right at the end, we saw the United their fans want to see. And when they came back from 2-0 down, they also had some momentum. But it didn’t last and they quickly reverted to their default way of playing, which is slow and negative – and before long they were 4-2 down.

 'The players need to understand the expectations' published at 19:43 GMT 19:43 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Ashley Young 
Former Man Utd winger on Sky Sports 
 Man United were a bit static. There needs to be so much more. The players need to understand when you come out here, what the fans expect is it's just a given to run, to work hard, to out run a team. 
 When you concede early you're on the back foot straight away. It's decisions that are being made that are not working and that are so easy to eradicate but you're not doing it so it's always going to be tough.

 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Roy Keane 
Former Manchester United captain on Sky Sports 
 There have been question marks over this time in terms of showing fight and desire. And as bad as this game was from a footballing point of view they kept going until the end.
 On the one hand it's dreadful to give up four goals at home. But they kept going so you have to give them a little bit of praise. 
 In terms of the bigger picture it's that rollercoaster of watching Manchester United. Some bits were so, so bad. Defensively, the way they started the first half and the way they started the second half. But they looked dead and buried so you have to give them a little bit of credit. Ultimately, still nowhere near good enough to try and get towards the middle of the table.

 'It's a learning experience today' published at 19:37 GMT 19:37 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa captain John McGinn, speaking to Sky Sports: "Obviously, in a very strong position to win the game. We've experienced it enough here, you need to defend until the 95th minute and beyond. We didn't manage the first half enough. We have a very young team and it's a learning experience today. 
 "We were pretty comfortable, to be honest, and then the third goal goes in. I've seen it more than the fourth. It's very naive. We need to defend it better as a team. It's a very poor goal. We're a very inexperienced team at the moment. It's a harsh lesson and one we need to learn from fast. 
 On Villa's poor Old Trafford record potentially playing a part: "Not for those moments, if you're playing against any team in the Premier League, you need to stay focused for the team. We gave them a chance to get the corner again. We need to get tighter. I haven't seen it back properly, so I don't know if it's a foul or not on the goalkeeper, but it gives them the chance to equalise."

 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa

Former Republic of Ireland midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 I think the problem runs deeper than Michael Carrick. I think he'll take his share of the responsibility for it, no doubt about it, and the players have to as well. 
 And when they step out on the pitch they can't be making the mistakes that they are, if you some of the mistakes they made tonight in an under-15s game you'd be disappointed.
 They need to sort that out. But it runs deeper. There's football leadership, ownership and financial issues that need resolving, there's a bigger picture at the moment.

 'I don't like situation but we can do something about it' published at 19:24 GMT 19:24 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, speaking to Sky Sports: 
 "Disappointed not to win the game. We were the better team for large parts. Made it difficult for ourselves with the goals we're giving away. Not just one but two in succession to put us in a difficult position. We did it the other night, did it again today, come back into the game and then could've won it at the end.
 "It's just moments we need to tighten up on, different moments in the game and we're giving teams goals that they don't normally get in the game. We tighten up on that then there's a lot of good in that performance. I thought we were the better team but conceding the goals that we are is not helping us at all.
 "No goal is a good goal to concede but there are ones you can do a bit more about and the ones we gave away today we have to tighten it up. It's making it difficult for ourselves and giving ourselves too much to do in games but we did a lot and still feel we should have won the game."
 On conceding so many goals: "There's been too many - that is clear and we know that. Something we have to put right.
 "I liked the character, the quality of football. We had most of the game, attacked the box we had shots and created chances. Coming from a place where you're 2-0 down and haven't had a good run of results the boys played good football - pressed well. A lot of the game was where we want it but if you look at it overall there's a lot [to like] and to finish the game and never give up it shows the character in the boys."
 On fans: "They are right behind the players, they are desperate to get behind us and for us to give something. There's frustration and disappointment at times and we all feel that but they're right behind the boys, they were until the end today and we all feel that."
 On potential for relegation fight: "We're in November so I don't like the situation and the results we've had but we can definitely do something about it."

 'I am disappointed but we move on' published at 19:20 GMT 19:20 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "I am disappointed but we move on. I have to analyse this match. It is very important to analyse deeply. First half, we started very good, but they were pushing. We were resilient. We tried to change. We started very well, scoring two goals again. How we lost the last six minutes at the time, conceding two goals is very frustrating. It's a process. The keeper, as well, is adapting but he still has work to do and how we have to defend when they are blocking us. In another country, maybe it's a foul but here it's not. 
 "We were facing Manchester United at Old Trafford today. They are getting better. How we managed in the 90 minutes, we have to continue to improve and feel confident. How can we manage the first half and how can we stop them better than we did? 
 On if United would come back: "They have very good players and the atmosphere is always fantastic. They were feeling good and confident and playing Champions League. They will come back again."

 'We threw it away' published at 19:13 GMT 19:13 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa captain John McGinn, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "We have to manage these moments better. Not a lot of teams will come here 2-0 and give goals away. We have to defend better in those positions. In the last 10 minutes of each half, we have to manage better. 
 "We have a lot of inexperienced players but a lot of talent and that's why we score goals. It doesn't matter if United are low in confidence, you're always up against it. The third goal was really poor and gave them a lot of encouragement to score. 
 "We lost two points. We threw it away. The last five minutes were just madness. It's going to sting. 
 "The manager is a winner; he'll be hurting the way we are. We go play international football but he'll dwell on it for two weeks."

 'We have lost two points today' published at 19:07 GMT 19:07 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports: 
 "A very difficult match. We competed well and we struggled in the first half after our two goals. Second half we had good balance to try to win the match. Scored two more goals and when we were controlling the game in the last six minutes they scored two goals. They can do it - they did it against Roma. My analysis is that overall we have lost a good opportunity to win the match.
 "We have young talented players, we need to get this mix. We are being demanding to play at this level. United showed their level. We must continue working, move on and analyse and how we can defend better and in the moment we were dominating get the better attack. We are disappointed, frustrated because in miunute 90 we are winning 2-4. We will accept the result because we have won three and drawn three in last matches and we're doing well. But today we have lost two points.
 "We must be positive even in defeat because we have to continue moving on with the process."
 On storming off at the end: "They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I thought the match was finishing. 
 "Not unfair - they scored the goal and I thought the match was over."

 Figure caption, Man Utd score twice in stoppage-time to share points in eight-goal thriller
 By Gary Rose BBC Sport journalist Manchester United twice came back from two goals down to earn a point against Aston Villa in an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford, although they will go into the international break in the Premier League relegation zone. 
 The Red Devils had dropped into the bottom three following Nottingham Forest's win against Manchester City on Saturday, and the weekend continued to get worse for Michael Carrick's side as they found themselves 2-0 down against Villa after just four minutes.
 United fought back to be level at the break, but then conceded two goals in eight minutes at the start of the second half.
 That looked to have sucked the fight out of the home side but remarkably - and for the third time in a week after recovering to beat Roma on Tuesday - they came back from two goals behind again.
 Joshua Zirkzee sparked it when he struck two minutes into stoppage time to make it 4-3, before Patrick Dorgu dramatically levelled in the sixth minute added on when he headed in from a corner.
 They almost won it, too, but ultimately had to settle for snatching a draw from the jaws of defeat - leaving them 18th and one point from safety going into a two-week break.
 It was a result that will not quite ease the pressure on Carrick, given their at times chaotic defending, but he will be the happier of the two managers.
 Unai Emery's side had made a dream start when Alysson opened the scoring inside the opening minute as his shot squeezed under Senne Lammens, who moments later parried a second Alysson shot - with Nicolas Jackson there to fire in the loose ball.
 But Manchester United were awarded a penalty in the 14th minute when Boubacar Kamara took down Matheus Cunha inside the box, and Bruno Fernandes made no mistake from the spot.
 That seemed to galvanise the hosts and they were the better side for the rest of the half, deservedly drawing level just before the break when Youri Tielemans - who joined Manchester United from Villa in the summer - drove in from Noussair Mazraoui's cutback.
 However, all that work was undone as Manchester United conceded two further goals early in the second half.
 First, Aston Villa were given a spot-kick a minute after the break when Diogo Dalot took down Alysson and John McGinn stepped up to confidently convert.
 Leon Goretzka then restored Villa's two-goal advantage in the 53rd minute following some haphazard defending following a free-kick. Leny Yoro headed the ball back towards Lammens, who punched it on to his own crossbar and Goretzka was there to prod in at the back post.
 From then on it seemed like Villa would take a win that would lift them up to eighth, but then came the stoppage-time drama that will have provided some sense of relief for Carrick.
 Dorgu makes dramatic impact - Man Utd v Aston Villa ratings 
 Published 2 hours ago 
 Have your say on Man Utd’s performance 
 What did you learn from Aston Villa’s display? 
 Figure caption, 'We can't count out relegation'
 Man Utd analysis: Defensive frailties remain a concern 
 Fans will have certainly left Old Trafford entertained and, while this was a memorable game, Carrick will know Manchester United cannot keep putting themselves into positions of needing to stage fightbacks.
 Their defensive frailties have repeatedly left them in difficult situations, and Lammens should have done better for the first two goals against Villa, while defenders Dalot and Yoro were at fault for the third and fourth goals.
 United have to be commended for not giving up, both in this game and against Roma in the Champions League, but their defending has to improve if they are to end their search for a first Premier League win since August anytime soon.
 They have shipped 30 goals in all competitions this season - no side in Europe's top five leagues have conceded more.
 Figure caption, Michael Carrick post-match interview - Manchester United v Aston Villa
 Aston Villa analysis: Game management a concern 
 Emery was clearly exasperated at how his side twice gave up strong positions at Old Trafford, and he headed towards the tunnel the moment Manchester United equalised for the second time.
 The performance leaves big question marks over Aston Villa's game management, and it will have been concerning for Emery just how swiftly his players wilted after conceding the first and third goals.
 Villa should really have been celebrating a first win in four games but instead this extends their recent stumble, following an unbeaten seven-match run through September and October.
